newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ injects 200 bln yen into money market-traders.
newsitem.headline: BOJ injects 200 bln yen into money market-traders.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) injected a net 200 billion yen into the money market on Friday, money traders said.
It was the first time the BOJ had conducted an accommodative money market operation since August 7, 1996, traders said.
Before the operation the market had a fund shortfall of 100 billion yen.
The key overnight call rate fell to around 0.48 percent after the operation, down from the previous day's weighted average of 0.53 percent.
The BOJ's decision to adopt an accommodative money market stance had a significant impact on the market, a trust bank trader said.

"The market realized that an accommodative operation could take place at any time, but it still had a substantial impact because the BOJ had been conducting neutral money market operations for so long," a trust bank trader said.

A BOJ official said this morning's accommodative money market operation was aimed at lowering the key overnight call rate. The official added that the operation was in line with commitments announced in September 1995.

When the BOJ last cut its discount rate on September 8, 1995, to 0.50 percent from one percent, the bank said it expected the key overnight call rate on average to move slightly below the discount rate as it would make efforts to supply sufficient funds to the money market.
